methods.note: public -> protected, and setSecondsOnFire(8) -> igniteForSeconds(8). 1.20.4 Entity.setSecondsOnFire(i): j=i*20, for LivingEntity j=ProtectionEnchantment.getFireAfterDampener(this,j), set if remainingFireTicks<j. 1.20.5 Entity.igniteForSeconds(int i) = igniteForTicks(i*20), and LivingEntity.igniteForTicks overrides with super.igniteForTicks(ProtectionEnchantment.getFireAfterDampener(this,i)), Entity.igniteForTicks sets if remainingFireTicks<i: the same ticks and the same dampener
only adds a trailing boolean parameter, which the 1.21.10 body never reads (body: CLEAR_FREEZE, FIRE_IGNITE, runAfter hurt inFire, all unchanged)
1.12.2 returns the AABB constant collisionBox = new AABB(0,0,0,1,1,1) (1.12.2 Block line 95); 1.13.2 returns Shapes.block(), the unit cube VoxelShape. Same full-block box, only the shape type changes

calculateFace(dir) -> getFaceShape(dir). 1.14.4 VoxelShape.getFaceShape returns this for empty/Shapes.block(), else a per-direction cached result of the private calculateFace, whose body equals the 1.13.2 public calculateFace (same coords test, fuzzyEquals 1.0E-7, findIndex 0.9999999/1.0E-7, SliceShape). Shapes are immutable, so the cache returns the same shape

moved from Block/BlockState: 1.15.2 Block#getCollisionShape(state,getter,pos,ctx) is the same 'hasCollision ? arg.getShape(arg2,arg3) : Shapes.empty()'; 1.15.2 BlockState#getCollisionShape(getter,pos) and (getter,pos,ctx) have the same bodies with this instead of this.asState(), and 1.16 BlockState.asState() returns this
visibility only: public -> protected; the body is unchanged

the parameter Level becomes BlockGetter and an Entity parameter is added. The base body still returns Shapes.block() and ignores both, and the BlockStateBase wrapper only passes the arguments through to the block

moved from Block/BlockState: 1.15.2 Block#getShape(state,getter,pos,ctx) returns Shapes.block(); 1.15.2 BlockState#getShape(getter,pos) = getShape(getter,pos,CollisionContext.empty()) and getShape(getter,pos,ctx) = getBlock().getShape(this,...). Identical apart from this vs this.asState(), and 1.16 BlockState.asState() returns this
visibility only: public -> protected; the body is unchanged

moved to BlockBehaviour.BlockStateBase: the 1.16 getCollisionShape(getter,pos) has the same cache/collisionShape body and getCollisionShape(getter,pos,ctx) = getBlock().getCollisionShape(this.asState(),...), where asState() returns this (1.16 BlockState)
moved to BlockBehaviour.BlockStateBase with the identical body 'this.cache == null || this.cache.largeCollisionShape' (1.16 BlockBehaviour line 438)
moved to BlockBehaviour.BlockStateBase (1.16 line 698) with the same body 'cache != null ? cache.isFaceSturdy[dir.ordinal()] : Block.isFaceSturdy(this.asState(), ...)'; asState() returns this
visibility only: public -> protected; the body is unchanged
adds an InsideBlockEffectApplier parameter that is only passed on to super.entityInside; the base BlockBehaviour.entityInside is empty in both 1.21.4 and 1.21.5; the hurt logic is unchanged
adds a boolean parameter that is only passed on to super.entityInside; the base BlockBehaviour.entityInside is empty in both 1.21.9 and 1.21.10; the hurt logic is unchanged

the Guava Predicates.and(NO_SPECTATORS, anonymous) becomes NO_SPECTATORS.and(lambda): same order and same short-circuit, and the team and collision-rule logic is identical. One textual difference: the 1.12.2 inner apply(arg) shadowed the outer arg, so arg.level.isClientSide read the candidate's level, while the 1.13.2 lambda reads the pusher's level. The candidates come from the pusher's own level query, so this is the same Level object
arg.level -> arg.level(); 1.20 Entity.level() returns this.level
an instanceof pattern (Player lvx && lvx.isLocalPlayer()) replaces the cast, and locals are renamed (lvx->lv2x, lv2x->lv3); same conditions and team logic
level().isClientSide field -> isClientSide(); 1.21.9 Level.isClientSide() returns the private final isClientSide field

(6.0 + LEVEL * 3.0) / 16.0 is inlined from the new helper getPixelContentHeight(int i) = 6.0 + i * 3.0 (1.21.6), applied to the same unboxed LEVEL value and divided by 16.0: the identical double expression
a helper extracted from the 1.21.5 getContentHeight numerator: 6.0 + i * 3.0 is exactly the old (6.0 + LEVEL.intValue() * 3.0)
adds a BlockState parameter that is only passed to super.stepOn; Block.stepOn is empty in both 1.16.5 and 1.17; the fireImmune/frost-walker/hurt logic is unchanged
the parameter type Level becomes LevelReader; the body (getBlockEntity, then method_11701 or null) is unchanged
adds a CollisionContext parameter that the body ignores; the body is unchanged
visibility only: public -> protected; the body is unchanged
moved from the private PistonMovingBlockEntity.getMovementArea (1.14.4 line 208), whose body is identical (same step sign, min/max and per-direction AABB)

getDeltaX/Y/Z (1.14.4) are inlined. Each is POSITIVE ? a.maxK - b.minK : b.maxK - a.minK, so EAST/UP/SOUTH give a.max-b.min and WEST/DOWN/NORTH give b.max-a.min. The old default:Y branch and the new default:UP branch are unreachable (all axes and directions are covered). The method is also made static; it never used this

the slime velocity write velocityK = step becomes copying getDeltaMovement, replacing the one axis component and calling setDeltaMovement(e,g,h) (1.14.4: new Vec3 assigned to deltaMovement), so the same components result; the local e is renamed j; move(PISTON, x,y,z) becomes move(PISTON, new Vec3(x,y,z)) with the same products

this.getMovementArea -> PistonMath.getMovementArea (identical body, checked); index loops become for-each over the same lists in the same order; this.getMovement becomes the static getMovement (equivalent, checked); the NOCLIP.set / move(PISTON, new Vec3(i*step)) / NOCLIP.set(null) sequence moves into moveEntityByPiston(lv, entity, i, lv), whose body is exactly that sequence (1.15)

made static with explicit (level, pos, f, blockEntity). this.level/this.getBlockPos() become arg/arg2, which the 1.17 ticker passes as the block entity's own level and position (PistonMovingBlockEntity::tick). moveByPositionAndProgress and fixEntityWithinPistonBase become static with pos in place of worldPosition and the same arithmetic (checked in 1.16.5 and 1.17). The rest is the same
a helper extracted from the 1.14.4 moveCollidedEntities: NOCLIP.set(dir); move(MoverType.PISTON, new Vec3(d*stepX, d*stepY, d*stepZ)); NOCLIP.set(null), the identical statements
getBlock() == Blocks.MOVING_PISTON -> is(Blocks.MOVING_PISTON); in 1.16 BlockStateBase.is(Block) = getBlock().is(arg) and Block.is(Block) = this == arg

made static (level, pos, state, blockEntity), with this.level/worldPosition replaced by the arguments that the 1.17 ticker passes for this block entity, and this.x replaced by arg4.x; statements and constants are identical (84, 67, deathTicks < 5, +0.5F, clamp 1.0F), with calls to the equally refactored static moveCollidedEntities/moveStuckEntities
isClientSide field -> isClientSide(); 1.21.9 Level.isClientSide() returns the field

arg.getType().is(tag) -> entity.is(tag). In 26.1 Entity implements TypedInstance, whose is(TagKey) = typeHolder().is(tag), and typeHolder() = type.builtInRegistryHolder(); in 1.21.11 EntityType.is(tag) = builtInRegistryHolder.is(tag). Also a parameter rename
the instanceof cast becomes an instanceof pattern variable; same check and same call

java.util.Random -> RandomSource for level.getRandom(), used only inside the client-side particle block with the same draws (nextBoolean, two randomBetween); the stuck multiplier and the server logic are unchanged

public -> protected, and getFeetBlockState() -> getInBlockState(): a rename with the same body (lazy level().getBlockState(blockPosition()) cached in a field reset at the same places, 1.20.4 vs 1.20.5 Entity)
isClientSide field -> isClientSide(); 1.21.9 Level.isClientSide() returns the field
adds a boolean parameter that the body never reads (checked in the full 1.21.10 body); the local bl is renamed bl2
getGameRules().getBoolean(RULE_MOBGRIEFING) -> getGameRules().get(MOB_GRIEFING): the new GameRule<Boolean> mob_griefing (default true) returns the stored boolean value of the same rule
only parameters and locals are renamed (arg->state/level/pos/entity/effectApplier/isPrecise, lv->random, bl2->isMoving, lv2->position) and final is added; the statements are identical

state.get(FACING) -> getValue(FACING) (an accessor rename), and getEntitiesIn(null, box) -> getEntities(null, box). 1.12.2 Level.getEntitiesIn(e, box) = getEntities(e, box, NO_SPECTATORS), and 1.13.2 EntityGetter.getEntities(e, box) = getEntities(e, box, NO_SPECTATORS)
move(SHULKER_BOX, x, y, z) -> move(SHULKER_BOX, new Vec3(x, y, z)) with the same three products
an index loop becomes a for-each over the same list, in the same order

getProgressDeltaAabb(dir, from, to) -> getProgressDeltaAabb(1.0F, dir, from, to). With size 1.0F the 1.20.5 body starts from AABB(0,0,0,1,1,1), the same as the old new AABB(BlockPos.ZERO), and multiplies every expand/contract term by 1.0 (exact), so the box is the same
pos.getBottomCenter() -> Vec3.atBottomCenterOf(pos); 26.1.2 BlockPos.getBottomCenter() returns Vec3.atBottomCenterOf(this), and atBottomCenterOf/atLowerCornerWithOffset are identical in 26.2

PushReaction.IGNORE -> IGNORE_ENTITY: the 26.3 enum is renamed constant by constant, and exactly the same classes return it (AreaEffectCloud, ArmorStand marker, Display, Interaction, Marker, OminousItemSpawner; grep 26.2 vs 26.3)

this.doNeighborUpdates() -> static doNeighborUpdates(getLevel(), worldPosition, getBlockState()); 1.16.5 body getBlockState().updateNeighbourShapes(getLevel(), getBlockPos(), 3) and 1.17 body arg3.updateNeighbourShapes(arg, arg2, 3) with the same arguments

a legacy remap artefact: in 1.10.2 the inner block-state class decompiles to net/minecraft/state/StateManager$BlockStateImpl.java, where both overloads have the identical bodies (block.getCollisionShape(this, level, pos) and block.getShape(this, level, pos))
